set.st: Aug 1901: canal excavators found an iron chest ten feet down, first taken for petrified wood, holding about $4,000 in Spanish coins, many dated 1668 and some earlier. Pin is mile 20 measured along the feeder, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Hennepin Canal Feeder about 20 mi S of Sterling (1901 wire), measured along the feeder to sec 23 T18N R6E, Bureau Co
pinev: Measured along the OSM Hennepin Canal Feeder from Rock Falls (29.3 mi total): mile 20 = 41.527,-89.769, sec 23 T18N R6E (Fairfield Twp), Bureau Co; Tampico about 7 mi N, Manlius about 5 mi SE. r1500.

set.st: Legend (Des Moines Register 1927): a lone Indian fleeing pursuers in 1832 with a heavy two-lobed sack of plunder crossed a clearing on what became the Christopher Meyer farm; at a spring about half a mile on he was seen without the sack and was later shot. Meyer built his house between the clearing and the spring and dug for years; his daughter Dora (Mrs. Timmerman) and the school children hunted the hummocks. Pin is the Meyer farm on the 1886 atlas, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Christopher Meyer farm, NE¼ sec 10 T100N R5W, Union City Twp (1886 atlas), about 9 mi W of New Albin; the clearing and the spring half a mile on are not yet fixed
pinev: 1886 Allamakee Co atlas, Union City Twp: 'Christopher Meyer 160', NE¼ sec 10 T100N R5W, the same Christopher Meyer the story names.
School No. 1 about 1 mi SE and No. 7 about 1 mi SW on the 1886 plate; the 'community schoolhouse' clearing is one of these or a later school.

src: Atlas of Allamakee County, Iowa (1886), Union City Twp T100N R5W

pinev: From the Jan 1934 report: about 12 road miles east of Grand Rapids on US 2 (between Philbin and Warba) and 2 mi north; 3 km covers the 12-16 mile spread between reports.
Road-measured (OSRM) along US 2 east from Grand Rapids: mile 12 = 47.1458,-93.3207 (sec 19 T54N R23W, Feeley Twp).
2 mi N of that = 47.175,-93.321, sec 7 T54N R23W; pin there, r2000.
Straight-line alternative 47.266,-93.275 (sec 9 T55N R23W) if '12 miles' was not by road.
Placed from the source text: GNIS Pinckney (village)
1930 census: Patrick Dillon b. 1884 IN, Pinckney, a son b. 1917 New York, so the family came after 1917; no Dillon on the 1915 Putnam Twp plate. Farm not placed.

1932 local paper: the farm was formerly the Kearney homestead. Kearney is not on the 1875 or 1915 Putnam Twp plates; census shows John M. and Margaret Kearney in Putnam Twp 1870-1900 and Margaret in Pinckney village by 1910; deeds or probate needed.
